name: Yājñavalkya

realization_account.text: BAU 6.5.3 says the white Yajus formulas come from the sun (Āditya) and are proclaimed by Yājñavalkya Vājasaneya; later Purāṇic accounts elaborate that he received them from the sun (not recorded here in detail).
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

summary: The central teacher of the Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad: he teaches Maitreyī that the self is to be seen, heard, reflected on and meditated upon (BAU 2.4, 4.5), defeats the brahmins at Janaka's court (BAU 3) and teaches Janaka on light, dream, sleep, death and karma (BAU 4.3-4). BAU 6.5.3 names him Vājasaneya, through whom the white Yajus formulas received from the sun are proclaimed.
notes: Teacher of the mantha rite lineage: Uddālaka Āruṇi taught it to his pupil Yājñavalkya (BAU 6.3.7, moderate on the kaṇḍikā). The Yājñavalkya Smṛti and Yoga-Yājñavalkya are later works attributed to him (owned by other units).

name: Maitreyī
summary: One of Yājñavalkya's two wives, described as a discusser of brahman (brahmavādinī, BAU 4.5.1); when he is about to leave the household she refuses wealth that cannot make her immortal and receives the teaching on the self (BAU 2.4, 4.5).

name: Kātyāyanī
summary: Yājñavalkya's other wife, whose understanding was that of ordinary women (strīprajñā, BAU 4.5.1); the property is to be divided between her and Maitreyī (BAU 2.4.1, 4.5.2).

name: Uddālaka Āruṇi
summary: Brahmin teacher of the Gautama clan, father of Śvetaketu: teaches the doctrine of being (sat) with the refrain tat tvam asi (ChU 6); questions Yājñavalkya on the thread and the inner controller (BAU 3.7); goes as a pupil to Pravāhaṇa Jaivali (BAU 6.2; ChU 5.3), to Aśvapati Kaikeya (ChU 5.11) and to Citra (KauU 1.1).
notes: ChU 3.11.4 says his father taught him the honey-doctrine as the eldest son.

name: Śvetaketu Āruṇeya
summary: Son of Uddālaka Āruṇi; returns proud after twelve years of Vedic study and is taught being and tat tvam asi (ChU 6); cannot answer Pravāhaṇa Jaivali's five questions (BAU 6.2; ChU 5.3); sent to Citra (KauU 1.1).

name: Janaka of Videha
summary: King of Videha whose sacrifice is the setting of the debate at BAU 3; he reports six teachers' definitions of brahman (BAU 4.1) and is taught by Yājñavalkya on the self as light, dream, deep sleep and death (BAU 4.3-4); told 'you have reached fearlessness' (BAU 4.2.4).
notes: 'Janaka' is a dynastic name; other units record other Janakas (e.g., tch:daivarati-janaka).

name: Gārgī Vācaknavī
summary: Woman participant in the debate at Janaka's court: she questions Yājñavalkya on what the worlds are woven upon, is warned not to ask too much lest her head fall off (BAU 3.6), returns with two questions 'like two arrows', hears the teaching of the imperishable (akṣara) and declares that no one will defeat him (BAU 3.8).

name: Ajātaśatru of Kāśī
summary: King of Kāśī who refutes Gārgya Bālāki's twelve (KauU: sixteen) identifications of brahman and teaches the self into which the sleeping person withdraws, from which all breaths, worlds and gods come forth like sparks (BAU 2.1; KauU 4). He notes it is against the natural order for a brahmin to come to a kṣatriya to learn brahman.
notes: Distinct from the Magadhan king of the Buddhist texts; id disambiguated.

name: Gārgya Bālāki
summary: A proud (dṛpta) learned brahmin who offers to explain brahman to Ajātaśatru, proposes a series of persons in the sun, moon and other phenomena, is refuted and becomes his pupil (BAU 2.1; KauU 4).

name: Pravāhaṇa Jaivali
summary: King of the Pañcālas; asks Śvetaketu the five questions and teaches Gautama Āruṇi the doctrine of the five fires and the two paths, saying this knowledge had never before dwelt with brahmins (BAU 6.2; ChU 5.3-10); in ChU 1.8-9 he teaches that space (ākāśa) is the final support of the sāman.

name: Aśvapati Kaikeya
summary: King of the Kekayas who teaches five great householders and Uddālaka Āruṇi the vaiśvānara self as a whole, correcting each one's partial view (ChU 5.11-18); he claims there is no thief, miser, drunkard, man without a sacred fire, ignorant or adulterer in his kingdom (ChU 5.11.5).

name: Raikva 'with the cart' (sayugvan)
summary: A sage found scratching his sores under a cart, whom King Jānaśruti seeks out; he rebuffs the king's gifts, calling him śūdra, and teaches the saṃvarga ('gatherer') doctrine: wind among the deities and breath among the vital powers absorb all others (ChU 4.1-3).

name: Jānaśruti Pautrāyaṇa
summary: A great-grandson of Janaśruta, a generous giver who kept open houses for food; overhearing geese compare him unfavourably to Raikva, he seeks Raikva and receives the saṃvarga teaching (ChU 4.1-2).

name: Sanatkumāra
summary: Teacher of Nārada in ChU 7: leads him from name to plenitude (bhūman) and shows him 'the far shore beyond darkness'; 'they call him Skanda' (ChU 7.26.2).

name: Nārada
summary: The divine seer (devarṣi) who comes to Sanatkumāra learned in all the sciences yet 'a knower of mantras, not of the self', and in sorrow; he is taught the ladder to bhūman (ChU 7).
notes: Later traditions attach the Nārada Bhakti Sūtra and other works to a Nārada; this entry records only the Upaniṣadic figure.

name: Satyakāma Jābāla
summary: Son of Jabālā, who did not know his lineage; accepted as a pupil by Hāridrumata Gautama for telling the truth (ChU 4.4); taught the four quarters of brahman by a bull, fire, a goose and a diver-bird (ChU 4.5-9); teacher of Upakosala (ChU 4.10-15); in BAU 4.1.6 he holds that brahman is the mind.

name: Jabālā (mother of Satyakāma)
summary: Satyakāma's mother, who tells him she does not know his lineage because in her youth she went about much as a serving woman (paricāriṇī), and bids him call himself Satyakāma Jābāla (ChU 4.4.1-2).

name: Hāridrumata Gautama
summary: Teacher who accepts Satyakāma Jābāla because 'no non-brahmin could speak thus' and initiates him (ChU 4.4.3-5).

name: Upakosala Kāmalāyana
summary: Pupil of Satyakāma who tended his teacher's fires for twelve years; the fires themselves taught him 'breath is brahman, ka is brahman, kha is brahman' before his teacher taught him the person in the eye (ChU 4.10-15).

name: Śāṇḍilya
summary: Named author of the Śāṇḍilya-vidyā: all this is brahman; the self within the heart, smaller than a grain and greater than the worlds, is brahman, which 'I shall attain on departing' (ChU 3.14.1-4).
notes: The same teaching appears in Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa 10.6.3 (moderate). Later works (Śāṇḍilya Bhakti Sūtra, Śāṇḍilya Upaniṣad) are attributed to a Śāṇḍilya; identity not asserted here.

name: Dadhyañc Ātharvaṇa
summary: Seer who taught the honey-doctrine (madhu-vidyā) to the two Aśvins through a horse's head, as recounted with Ṛgvedic verses at BAU 2.5.16-19.

name: Bhṛgu Vāruṇi
summary: Son of Varuṇa who asks his father to teach him brahman and, by repeated tapas, realizes in turn that food, breath, mind, understanding and bliss are brahman (TU 3.1-6: 'the knowledge of Bhṛgu and Varuṇa').
notes: Contribution of lin:upanisadic; other units record the Purāṇic and astrological Bhṛgu.

name: Varuṇa (as teacher)
summary: The god Varuṇa as father-teacher of Bhṛgu: gives the definition of brahman as that from which beings are born, by which they live and into which they enter, and sends him to seek it by tapas (TU 3.1).

name: Pippalāda
summary: Sage of the Praśna Upaniṣad who answers the six questions of six seekers after making them live a year with austerity, celibacy and faith (PrU 1.2).
notes: Tradition connects him with the Paippalāda śākhā of the Atharvaveda (moderate).

name: Sukeśā Bhāradvāja
summary: One of the six seekers devoted to brahman who come to Pippalāda with fuel in hand; he asks about the person of sixteen parts (PrU 6).

name: Śaibya Satyakāma
summary: One of the six seekers devoted to brahman who come to Pippalāda with fuel in hand; he asks what world the one who meditates on Om until death wins (PrU 5); distinct from Satyakāma Jābāla.

name: Sauryāyaṇī Gārgya
summary: One of the six seekers devoted to brahman who come to Pippalāda with fuel in hand; he asks what sleeps and what wakes in a person and who sees dreams (PrU 4).

name: Kausalya Āśvalāyana
summary: One of the six seekers devoted to brahman who come to Pippalāda with fuel in hand; he asks whence prāṇa is born and how it enters and divides itself (PrU 3).

name: Bhārgava Vaidarbhi
summary: One of the six seekers devoted to brahman who come to Pippalāda with fuel in hand; he asks how many deities support a being (PrU 2).

name: Kabandhī Kātyāyana
summary: One of the six seekers devoted to brahman who come to Pippalāda with fuel in hand; he asks whence creatures are born (PrU 1).

name: Hiraṇyanābha Kausalya
summary: A prince of Kosala who asked Sukeśā about the person of sixteen parts; Sukeśā, not knowing, refused to answer falsely, since one who speaks untruth withers to the root (PrU 6.1).

name: Brahmā (as first teacher)
summary: The first of the gods, maker and protector of the world, who taught the knowledge of brahman to his eldest son Atharvan (MuU 1.1.1); the first link of teacher-lines (ChU 3.11.4, 8.15.1); in KauU 1.5-7 he questions the knower arriving in the brahma-world.

name: Atharvan
summary: Eldest son of Brahmā, who received brahmavidyā and passed it to Aṅgir (MuU 1.1.1-2).

name: Aṅgir
summary: Link in the Muṇḍaka's line: received brahmavidyā from Atharvan and taught Satyavāha Bhāradvāja (MuU 1.1.2).

name: Satyavāha Bhāradvāja
summary: Link in the Muṇḍaka's line: from Aṅgir to Aṅgiras, handing on the knowledge 'higher and lower' (MuU 1.1.2).

name: Aṅgiras (teacher of Śaunaka)
summary: Teacher of the Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad: answers Śaunaka's question 'by knowing what is all this known?' with the higher and lower knowledge (MuU 1.1.3-5); 'this truth the seer Aṅgiras declared of old' (MuU 3.2.11).
notes: Whether tradition identifies him with the Ṛgvedic seer-family ancestor Aṅgiras is not asserted here.

name: Śaunaka Mahāśāla
summary: 'Śaunaka, the great householder', who approached Aṅgiras in the proper way and asked by knowing what all this becomes known (MuU 1.1.3).

name: Naciketas

realization_account.text: KU 2.3.18: having received this knowledge from Death and the whole rule of yoga, Naciketas attained brahman and became free of stain and death.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

summary: Boy who, given to Death by his father, waits three nights in Yama's house and chooses as his third boon the knowledge of what happens after death; refusing all worldly gifts, he receives the teaching of the self and the whole method of yoga and attains brahman (KU 1.1-2.3.18).

name: Yama (Mṛtyu)
summary: Death, lord of the dead, as teacher of Naciketas: grants three boons, tests him with offers of long life, wealth and pleasures, and teaches the good and the pleasant, Om, the unborn self, the chariot, the ladder to the person and yoga (KU).

name: Vājaśravasa (father of Naciketas)
alt_names: Uśan (some read uśan in KU 1.1.1 as a name)
summary: Naciketas's father, who in the Viśvajit sacrifice gives away all his possessions, offering worn-out cows; in anger he gives his son to Death (KU 1.1.1-4). Yama calls him Auddālaki Āruṇi (KU 1.1.11) and Naciketas calls him Gautama (KU 1.1.10).
notes: Whether he is the Uddālaka Āruṇi of ChU/BAU is not settled; KU 1.1.11 calls him Auddālaki ('son of Uddālaka').

name: Prajāpati (as teacher)
summary: Lord of creatures, teacher of gods, humans and asuras: teaches 'da' (BAU 5.2); teaches Indra and Virocana the self free from evil over 101 years (ChU 8.7-12); link in teacher-lines (ChU 3.11.4, 8.15.1); in MaiU 2 he teaches the Vālakhilyas.

name: Indra (as student and teacher)
summary: Lord of the gods: lives 101 years as Prajāpati's student and alone goes beyond the body-self (ChU 8.7-12); in the Kena he meets Umā Haimavatī and first knows the yakṣa as brahman (Kena 3.11-4.3); teaches Pratardana 'I am breath, the intelligent self' (KauU 3).

name: Virocana
summary: Lord of the asuras who studies with Prajāpati alongside Indra, concludes that the body is the self and teaches the asuras this 'doctrine of the asuras' (ChU 8.8.4-5).

name: Umā Haimavatī
summary: The very beautiful woman who appears to Indra in the sky where the yakṣa vanished and tells him it was brahman, in whose victory the gods had been glorifying themselves (Kena 3.12-4.1).
notes: Later Śākta and Śaiva readers identify her with the Goddess Umā/Pārvatī, daughter of Himavat.

name: Citra Gāṅgyāyani
alt_names: Citra Gārgyāyaṇi (reading of the Advaita-Śāradā text)
summary: A king who, about to sacrifice, questions Śvetaketu on the closed place of the world, then teaches Āruṇi (who comes fuel in hand) the path to the world of brahman (KauU 1.1-7).

name: Pratardana Daivodāsi
summary: Son of Divodāsa, who reached Indra's abode by fighting and valour and asked Indra for the boon most beneficial to humans; taught that Indra is breath, the intelligent self (KauU 3.1-2); the 'inner agnihotra of Pratardana' is named after him (KauU 2.5).

name: Śākāyanya
summary: Sage who teaches King Bṛhadratha the knowledge of the self in the Maitrī Upaniṣad, relaying what Prajāpati taught the Vālakhilyas.

name: Bṛhadratha
summary: A king of the Ikṣvāku line who, having installed his son and renounced his kingdom, practised austerities in the forest and asked Śākāyanya about the self, lamenting the foulness of the body and the transience of all things (MaiU 1.2-4).

name: Śvetāśvatara

realization_account.text: SU 6.21: by tapas and the grace of God (devaprasāda) he knew brahman.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

summary: The sage named at SU 6.21: by the power of austerity and by God's grace he knew brahman and declared it to the renunciants beyond the stages of life (atyāśramin).
notes: The name may be that of a Vedic school; historicity is unknown.

name: Ghora Āṅgirasa
summary: Teacher who taught Kṛṣṇa, son of Devakī, the doctrine of the person as sacrifice and the three sayings to be taken as refuge at death (ChU 3.17.6).

name: Kṛṣṇa Devakīputra
summary: 'Kṛṣṇa, son of Devakī', pupil of Ghora Āṅgirasa, who on hearing the teaching became free from thirst (ChU 3.17.6).
notes: Later tradition, and some scholars, identify him with Kṛṣṇa Vāsudeva of the Gītā (tch:krsna); the Upaniṣad says only 'Kṛṣṇa, son of Devakī'. Kept as a separate id; identification not asserted.

name: Aśvala
summary: Janaka's hotṛ priest, the first to question Yājñavalkya at the court debate, on how the sacrificer is freed from death, day and night, the fortnights (BAU 3.1).

name: Jāratkārava Ārtabhāga
summary: Questions Yājñavalkya on the eight graspers and over-graspers and on what remains of a person at death; they go aside and speak of karma (BAU 3.2).

name: Bhujyu Lāhyāyani
summary: Asks Yājñavalkya where the descendants of Parikṣit went (BAU 3.3); he had heard of it in Madra from a gandharva.

name: Uṣasti Cākrāyaṇa
summary: Asks Yājñavalkya to explain the brahman that is immediate and direct, the self within all (BAU 3.4, as Uṣasta); in ChU 1.10-11 he survives a famine among the Kurus by eating an elephant-keeper's leftover beans but refuses the leftover water, and then instructs priests on the deities of the chant.
notes: Identity of the BAU Uṣasta and the ChU Uṣasti is assumed from the shared patronymic (moderate).

name: Kahola Kauṣītakeya
summary: Asks Yājñavalkya the same question as Uṣasta and is told of the self beyond hunger, thirst, sorrow, delusion, old age and death, knowing which brahmins renounce the three desires (BAU 3.5.1).

name: Vidagdha Śākalya
summary: The last and most aggressive challenger at Janaka's court: questions Yājñavalkya on the number of gods and the persons and their abodes; unable to answer the question about the person of the Upaniṣads, his head shatters (BAU 3.9). In BAU 4.1.7 he holds that brahman is the heart.

name: Patañcala Kāpya
summary: Man of Madra in whose house Uddālaka studied the sacrifice; through a gandharva possessing his wife they learned of the thread and the inner controller (BAU 3.7.1).

name: Jitvan Śailini
summary: One of the teachers whose view Janaka reports to Yājñavalkya: brahman is speech (BAU 4.1.2); Yājñavalkya says he taught only its abode, not its support.

name: Udaṅka Śaulbāyana
summary: One of the teachers whose view Janaka reports to Yājñavalkya: brahman is breath (BAU 4.1.3); Yājñavalkya says he taught only its abode, not its support.

name: Barku Vārṣṇa
summary: One of the teachers whose view Janaka reports to Yājñavalkya: brahman is sight (BAU 4.1.4); Yājñavalkya says he taught only its abode, not its support.

name: Gardabhīvipīta Bhāradvāja
summary: One of the teachers whose view Janaka reports to Yājñavalkya: brahman is hearing (BAU 4.1.5); Yājñavalkya says he taught only its abode, not its support.

name: Prācīnaśāla Aupamanyava
summary: One of the five great householders and great Vedic scholars who asked 'what is our self, what is brahman?' and, with Uddālaka Āruṇi, went to Aśvapati Kaikeya; each had venerated only one part of the vaiśvānara self (ChU 5.11-17).

name: Satyayajña Pauluṣi
summary: One of the five great householders and great Vedic scholars who asked 'what is our self, what is brahman?' and, with Uddālaka Āruṇi, went to Aśvapati Kaikeya; each had venerated only one part of the vaiśvānara self (ChU 5.11-17).

name: Indradyumna Bhāllaveya
summary: One of the five great householders and great Vedic scholars who asked 'what is our self, what is brahman?' and, with Uddālaka Āruṇi, went to Aśvapati Kaikeya; each had venerated only one part of the vaiśvānara self (ChU 5.11-17).

name: Jana Śārkarākṣya
summary: One of the five great householders and great Vedic scholars who asked 'what is our self, what is brahman?' and, with Uddālaka Āruṇi, went to Aśvapati Kaikeya; each had venerated only one part of the vaiśvānara self (ChU 5.11-17).

name: Buḍila Āśvatarāśvi
summary: One of the five great householders and great Vedic scholars who asked 'what is our self, what is brahman?' and, with Uddālaka Āruṇi, went to Aśvapati Kaikeya; each had venerated only one part of the vaiśvānara self (ChU 5.11-17).

name: Śilaka Śālāvatya
summary: One of three experts on the udgītha who discuss the support of the sāman (ChU 1.8).

name: Caikitāyana Dālbhya
summary: One of three experts on the udgītha who discuss the support of the sāman (ChU 1.8).

name: Śaunaka Kāpeya
summary: Being served food with Abhipratārin Kākṣaseni when a student begs from them and speaks of the one god who swallowed four great ones (ChU 4.3.5-7).

name: Abhipratārin Kākṣaseni
summary: Companion of Śaunaka Kāpeya in the saṃvarga episode (ChU 4.3.5-7).

name: Mahidāsa Aitareya
summary: Knowing the person as sacrifice, he said to sickness 'why do you afflict me? I shall not die of this' and lived 116 years (ChU 3.16.7); the tradition regards him as the seer of the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa and Āraṇyaka.

name: Vāmadeva

realization_account.text: AU 2.1.5-6: while still in the womb he knew the births of the gods; knowing thus, on the body's breaking he rose up and became immortal.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

summary: The Ṛgvedic seer who, seeing that he was brahman, declared 'I was Manu, I was the sun' (BAU 1.4.10) and who, lying in the womb, knew all the births of the gods (AU 2.1.5, quoting RV 4.27.1).

name: Satyavacas Rāthītara
summary: Holds that truth (satya) is what matters (TU 1.9).

name: Taponitya Pauruśiṣṭi
summary: Holds that austerity (tapas) is what matters (TU 1.9).

name: Nāka Maudgalya
summary: Holds that Vedic study and teaching alone matter, for that is austerity (TU 1.9).

name: Triśaṅku
summary: Seer whose declaration after realization, beginning 'I am the mover of the tree', is recorded as 'the Veda-recitation of Triśaṅku' (TU 1.10).

name: Māhācamasya
summary: Knew the fourth vyāhṛti, mahaḥ, as brahman, the self, of which bhūḥ, bhuvaḥ and suvaḥ are the limbs (TU 1.5.1).

name: Kauṣītaki
summary: Taught 'breath is brahman' (KauU 2.1); as Sarvajit Kauṣītaki he had three worships of the sun (KauU 2.7).

name: Paiṅgya
summary: Taught 'breath is brahman' with the ordering of the senses (KauU 2.2).

name: Ayāsya Āṅgirasa
summary: Identified with the breath in the mouth, the essence (rasa) of the limbs, in the udgītha passages (BAU 1.3.8, 1.3.19; ChU 1.2.12).

name: Sāmaśravas
summary: Yājñavalkya's pupil, told to drive home Janaka's thousand cows (BAU 3.1.2).

name: Tura Kāvaṣeya
summary: Near the head of the final teacher-line of the BAU, receiving from Prajāpati (BAU 6.5.4).

name: Kapila
summary: Lineage contribution of lin:upanisadic: SU 5.2 speaks of 'the seer Kapila (or: the tawny seer) born in the beginning, whom he filled with knowledge'. Later tradition reads this as the Sāṃkhya founder, others as Hiraṇyagarbha; the Upaniṣad does not say which.

name: Manu
summary: Lineage contribution of lin:upanisadic: link in the teacher-lines Brahmā -> Prajāpati -> Manu -> creatures (ChU 3.11.4, 8.15.1); Vāmadeva says 'I was Manu' (BAU 1.4.10).
